title: Postquant Labs Launches QuipSwap Bridgeless Protocol for Quantum-Safe Cross-Chain Transactions - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Postquant Labs publicly launched QuipSwap, a bridgeless peer-to-peer atomic swap protocol built with quip.network that removes bridges, oracles, and wrapped assets to reduce classical DeFi exploit surface and deploys beta quantum-resistant wallets on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana ahead of anticipated quantum threats to legacy public-key signatures.

themes.theme: Bridgeless swap architecture as a security play

insights.claim: QuipSwap eliminates smart-contract bridges, oracles, liquidity pools, and wrapped assets — components the article identifies as historically targeted in major DeFi exploits — replacing them with a synchronized peer-to-peer atomic key exchange where claiming one side of a trade automatically releases the counterparty's claim key.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions QuipSwap against a well-documented DeFi attack surface (bridge hacks); investors evaluating cross-chain infrastructure should weigh whether removing custodial/oracle components meaningfully reduces exploit risk versus prior bridge protocols.
insights.quote: removes centralized intermediaries, smart contract bridges, oracles, and wrapped assets—components historically targeted in major decentralized finance (DeFi) exploits
insights.locator: Decentralized quantum network developer Postquant Labs

insights.claim: The QuipSwap codebase underwent a formal security audit by Oak Security following a live demonstration at ETHDenver, ahead of its public release, suggesting the team pursued third-party validation before going live rather than launching unaudited.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A completed third-party audit is a concrete, checkable diligence signal for investors or integrators assessing counterparty/protocol risk before relying on QuipSwap for cross-chain settlement.
insights.quote: the core codebase underwent a formal security audit conducted by Oak Security ahead of its public release

themes.theme: Quantum-resistant wallet rollout across major chains

insights.claim: Postquant Labs argues that quantum computers threaten public-key signature schemes such as ECDSA used across legacy blockchains, and has responded by deploying beta quantum-resistant wallets across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana while letting users retain native assets on existing chains.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete early-stage evidence of the 'quantum threat to crypto' narrative moving from theory to shipped (beta) product across the three largest smart-contract/payment chains — a space to watch for how major chains eventually respond to post-quantum migration pressure.
insights.quote: quantum computers threaten public-key signatures (such as ECDSA) across legacy blockchains, Postquant Labs has deployed beta quantum-resistant wallets across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana
insights.locator: Quantum-Resistant Wallet Deployment Across Major Chains

insights.claim: Postquant Labs, led by CEO Colton Dillion and CTO Dr. Richard Carback, is building quip.network as a decentralized marketplace connecting classical and quantum computing operators, positioning QuipSwap as one application layered on top of that broader quantum-compute marketplace infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals Postquant's business model extends beyond a single swap protocol to a marketplace connecting quantum and classical compute — worth tracking whether quip.network gains real transaction volume or customer adoption as evidence of the broader thesis.
insights.locator: Led by CEO Colton Dillion and CTO Dr. Richard Carback
